name: Óscar Romero
summary: Romero defended the poor, workers’ organizing, land reform, and human dignity against oligarchic privilege and state repression. His Christian vision combined structural social change with traditional marital and anti-abortion teachings, favoring nonviolent action while allowing narrowly limited resistance to tyranny.

unions-good.rationale: He explicitly defends strong rural and urban unions and their organizing rights.

property-fundamental.rationale: He explicitly denies that private property is absolute, subordinating it to social needs.

worker-ownership.rationale: He celebrates a court’s transfer of an insolvent mine to collective worker ownership.

empower-police-military.rationale: He opposes additional military equipment and training for the repressive Salvadoran forces.

traditional-family.rationale: He calls faithful marriage and family life fundamental to social peace.

abortion-legal.rationale: His own editorials oppose decriminalizing deliberately induced abortion, including proposed exceptions.

more-religion-public.rationale: He insists Christian faith must shape public struggles for justice rather than retreat from society.

revolution-justified.rationale: He permits insurrection exceptionally against prolonged tyranny, with strict limits.

democracy-best.rationale: He advocates democratic government protecting fundamental rights and a just economic order.

political-violence-never.rationale: He accepts proportionate defensive violence after peaceful remedies have been exhausted.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: He grounds care for nature in a covenant with God, alongside human dependence on it.

limit-population.rationale: He condemns population-control campaigns promoting sterilization and abortion.

means-match-ends.rationale: He rejects doing evil for good ends and prioritizes nonviolent justice.

total-state.rationale: He condemns subjecting the individual completely to the state.

national-self-determination.rationale: He defends peoples’ right to choose their own economic and political course.

reason-over-faith.rationale: He explicitly makes Christian revelation a guide to political judgment and action.

class-collaboration.rationale: He urges employers and unions to negotiate a fair share of their joint production.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: He describes ruling officers as unscrupulous servants of oligarchic interests.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: He demands punishment of those responsible for repression and compensation for victims’ families.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: He teaches that every man and woman deserves dignity as a child of God.

consent-of-governed.rationale: He identifies the people as the ultimate source of political power.

priority-to-poor.rationale: His political theology makes justice for the poor the overriding institutional priority.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: He rejects national-security claims used to justify arbitrary detention, torture, and repression.

clerical-rule.rationale: He insists the church must not turn itself into a political power.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: He makes the common good the standard governing private ownership.

land-redistribution.rationale: He praises redistribution from seven landowners to hundreds of campesino families.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: He conditionally legitimizes resistance to tyranny that destroys rights and the common good.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: He calls on privileged elites to share their wealth and enable just social change.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: He insists faith requires involvement in the public struggle for justice.

military-guardian-role.rationale: He condemns military command’s unconstitutional control of the country’s political course.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: He condemns divorce and teaches that marriage cannot be dissolved by human choice.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: He condemns possessiveness and wealth worship as destructive to solidarity and human fulfillment.

non-intervention.rationale: His Carter letter rejects foreign military, economic, and diplomatic pressure determining Salvadorans’ future.

religion-illusion.rationale: He defends transcendent faith as a source of effective liberation, rejecting its dismissal as consolation.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: He rejects oppressive capitalism and atheistic Marxism, proposing Christian social justice.

suppress-opposition.rationale: He denounces repression of independent political parties, unions, and popular associations.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: He explicitly supports the existence of armed forces and genuine public-security institutions.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: He condemns wealthy minorities’ disproportionate influence over laws and political participation.

independent-unions.rationale: He warns unions against manipulation by interests unrelated to workers.

person-over-state.rationale: He insists that law and political liberation must serve human dignity.

spiritual-nature.rationale: He presents liberation as personal, communal, and transcendent, beyond material improvement alone.

premarital-sex.rationale: He endorses the condemnation of premarital sex and marital infidelity.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: He expressly says Genesis’s creation of woman is a parable, not literal history.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: He explicitly denies any obligation to obey an immoral law or murderous order.

notes: Mature 1977–1980 teaching takes precedence over his earlier conservative reputation. Papal and conciliar passages count where he explicitly adopts and applies them, rather than merely because he was a Catholic bishop. His preference for nonviolence does not erase the express exceptions in his 1978 letter. Support for particular land transfers and a worker-owned mine does not establish a comprehensive socialist ownership program. General concern for the poor does not determine particular tax rates, healthcare entitlements, minimum-wage levels, or pension designs. Environmental concern does not establish a climate policy or a preferred pollution-control instrument. No views of later political movements are assigned to him.
